issues.legal_issue: Income received by a wakf manager is taxable at the maximum rate when the beneficiaries’ individual shares are indeterminate.
material_facts: The wakf deed directed the manager to use income for maintenance of family members, religious ceremonies, charitable purposes, and other expenses, and to invest any surplus in income-producing property.
The deed specified no individual shares in the income; beneficiaries had a right to maintenance according to their requirements, with allocation left to the manager’s discretion.
The income was assessed through the wakf’s manager, and the dispute concerned whether the first proviso to section 41(1) applied.
issues.conclusion: The beneficiaries’ individual shares were indeterminate under the deed, so the income was assessable at the maximum rate under the first proviso to section 41(1).
issues.legal_principle: Under section 41(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, income received by a trustee on behalf of beneficiaries is generally assessed as it would be in the beneficiaries’ hands. The first proviso requires assessment at the maximum rate where the beneficiaries’ individual shares are indeterminate or unknown. Shares are indeterminate where a deed grants only a right to maintenance according to requirements and leaves allocation to the manager’s discretion; the fact that beneficiaries can be identified does not establish specified shares.

rule.if: trust_income_tax_assessment and deed_grants_only_maintenance_rights and manager_controls_allocation and deed_specifies_no_individual_shares

predicates.trust_income_tax_assessment: An income-tax assessment concerns income received by a manager under a trust arrangement on behalf of beneficiaries.
predicates.deed_grants_only_maintenance_rights: The deed gives beneficiaries a right to maintenance according to their requirements rather than a defined share of income.
predicates.manager_controls_allocation: The deed leaves the allocation of income among beneficiaries to the manager’s discretion.
predicates.deed_specifies_no_individual_shares: The deed does not expressly or by necessary implication specify each beneficiary’s share of income.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment concerns trust income and the deed gives only discretionary maintenance rights without specifying individual shares, the income is assessed at the maximum rate.

issues.legal_issue: A wakf manager receives income on behalf of the beneficiaries for purposes of assessment through a trustee, notwithstanding the ideal vesting of wakf property in the Almighty.
material_facts: The respondent argued that wakf property vested in the Almighty and that the manager therefore received income on behalf of the Almighty rather than on behalf of a person.
The deed directed the manager to administer the property and use its income for the stated purposes and beneficiaries.
The governing income-tax provision expressly included trustees under qualifying wakf deeds and treated the manager as a trustee for assessment purposes.
issues.conclusion: The manager received the income on behalf of the beneficiaries, not the Almighty, and the income-tax provision applied to the wakf.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4 of the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, 1913, recognize wakfs benefiting family members, provided the required ultimate benefit is reserved, and permit that benefit to be postponed. Under Mahomedan law, the vesting of wakf property in the Almighty is ideal in sense; the manager uses the income for the benefit of the beneficiaries. Jewun Doss Sahoo v. Shah Kubeer-ood-deen explained that wakf property is treated as divine property because its benefit accrues to God’s creatures. Section 41(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, expressly treats the manager of a qualifying wakf as a trustee for assessment, so Mahomedan law does not exclude the wakf from that provision.

predicates.wakf_income_tax_assessment: An income-tax assessment concerns income received by a manager administering a wakf.
predicates.manager_administers_property_for_benefic: The manager administers the property for the benefit of persons provided for by the wakf.
predicates.income_used_for_beneficiaries_or_stated_: The manager applies the income to the beneficiaries or to purposes specified by the wakf.

issues.definition: When a wakf manager administers property and applies its income for beneficiaries or stated purposes, the manager receives that income on behalf of the beneficiaries.
